11 · Q4 Pulse 3: draft codebook for the conversation path chart

How did the chats unfold after the first message? A DRAFT codebook for your review

Denicia Aragon Espinosa

November 05, 2026

What this step does

You want a flow chart with three columns that shows how each chat unfolded:

  1. What the person first asked for (their opening request).
  2. What they did in their 2nd message.
  3. When they shared background information such as age, health history, medicines, how long it has been going on, or other conditions or symptoms.

Before we can count anything for columns 2 and 3, we need clear rules for each label. This is called a codebook.

This report is that codebook, in draft form. It also includes a first draft of the labels for all 52 chats, so you can see how the rules work on real messages.

Nothing here is final. The column 2 and 3 labels were drafted by the analyst assistant to test the rules. After you review the rules, the chats will be coded properly, as in step 10.

All quotes are from the de-identified conversations.

Column 1: the opening request (final)

This column is already done. It uses your final request types from step 10, grouped into three simple groups:

  • Asking to understand: Why is this happening, What is this, Explain my test results.
  • Asking what to do: How do I handle this problem, Should I see a doctor or get a test, Help me reach a health goal.
  • Just sharing information: Shared information, no question asked.

Your rule: if a chat asked both to understand and what to do, it goes to Asking what to do, because the action question is what the person really wants. This applied to 2 chats (6144ea17 and 69f441ce).

c1 |>
  mutate(pct = pct1(n / 52)) |>
  select(`Opening request` = group, Chats = n, `% of 52` = pct) |>
  gt()
Opening request Chats % of 52
Asking to understand 26 50.0%
Asking what to do 17 32.7%
Just sharing information 9 17.3%

Column 2: the person’s 2nd message (draft)

Which message counts? It is the next message the person wrote after their coded first message. For the 3 chats where we skipped a greeting (the first-real-message rule), the 2nd message is the one after the real first message.

Messages that only say thanks or “Nice” are skipped, and the next real message is used. This is the same idea as the first-real-message rule.

If the 2nd message has background information and a new question, the question decides column 2. The background still counts in column 3.

Each chat gets one label.

defs |>
  filter(column == "column 2") |>
  select(Label = name, `What it means` = definition, Include = include,
         `Do not include` = exclude, `Close calls` = close_call) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(Label ~ px(160))
Label What it means Include Do not include Close calls
Kept asking to understand The 2nd message asks a new question to understand something: what it is, why it happens, what it means, how long it lasts, how to tell, how likely. Questions about causes, meaning, test findings, duration, likelihood or general facts, even if background information is mentioned along the way (question wins). Questions that ask the AI about its own experience or opinion (for example survey-style questions) [P8]. Questions about what to do, take, change, or whether to see a doctor or get a test (M2). Statements with no new question (M3). 'How can I tell if I have X' is understanding (M1); 'Should I get checked for X' is action (M2). If both are asked, M2 wins. Practical 'how likely' questions (for example hospital bed availability) are M1. A question to the AI about itself is M1, not M6 [P8].
Then asked what to do The 2nd message asks for action: what to do, take or change, whether to see a doctor or specialist, which tests to get, whether something is safe, or what to do if a new symptom appears. Treatment, self-care, medicines, care-seeking, tests, plans, safety and 'what if I have this symptom' questions. Wins over M1 when both are asked. Questions that only ask what something is or why (M1). Pushback on the AI's advice (M4). A message that adds information and then asks 'What should I do?' is M2 (the question wins; any background information still counts in column 3).
Shared more about themselves The 2nd message mainly gives more information, with no new question: background information (age, health history, medicines, how long, other conditions or symptoms, weight, height, activity level or regular habits) and/or more description of the main problem, for themselves or the person they are asking for. Answers to the AI's follow-up questions; extra background offered on their own; information about a child, partner or parent they are asking for. Messages that also ask a real new question (M1 or M2). Messages saying the AI was wrong (M4). Continuing a task such as re-submitting a draft (M6). Adding a fact the AI did not know (for example the cause of their anemia) is M3, unless they say the AI got it wrong (M4). Only background information moves the chat into column 3 groups 1 to 3. More description of the main problem is M3 but is not background information for column 3.
Pushed back or questioned the AI The 2nd message disagrees with, corrects or challenges the AI, says it missed or misunderstood something, or asks it to check itself. 'You are missing?', 'that's not right', 'are you sure?', asking the AI to re-check earlier information. Simply adding new information without saying the AI was wrong (M3). If the main move is correcting the AI, code M4 even if a question follows.
Continued a task The 2nd message carries on a task the person started, such as re-submitting an edited version of a text for more help, without a new health question. Re-pasted or revised drafts, follow-up edits to a document. New questions (M1, M2), new information about themselves (M3), corrections of the AI (M4). Small label (1 chat); kept by researcher choice.
Stopped after one message There is no real participant message after the coded first message. Chats that end after the AI's answer; chats where the only later messages are thanks or acknowledgements. Any later message with a question, information, pushback or a task (M1 to M4, M6). 'Nice' or 'Ok thank you' alone does not count as a 2nd message. If a turn starts with a thanks or task fragment (for example 'Convert to PDF') but then gives real content, ignore the fragment and code the rest of the turn [P7].

Column 3: when they shared background information (draft)

This column is only for chats whose 2nd message was Then asked what to do or Shared more about themselves. Other chats end at column 2.

Background information means age, health history, other conditions, medicines, how long the problem has been going on, or other symptoms. The main complaint itself (“my foot hurts”) does not count. We record the first time background information appears.

We say “background information” rather than “personal details”, because “personal” could mean anything.

defs |>
  filter(column == "column 3") |>
  select(Label = name, `What it means` = definition, Include = include,
         `Do not include` = exclude, `Close calls` = close_call) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(Label ~ px(160))
Label What it means Include Do not include Close calls
With the first message The coded first message already contains background information about the person the question is about (themselves or someone they care for). Age, body weight, height, activity level and regular habits (for example 'I run daily', 'mostly sedentary') [P1], health history, other conditions, medicines, how long the problem has existed overall [P5], other symptoms beyond the problem asked about [P6], and recent events or care that led up to it, including something that happened before it started (for example travel, 'after sleeping', a doctor visit, a referral, prism glasses) [P3]. The main complaint on its own ('my foot is hurting', 'I have a tummy ache'). General or hypothetical questions. A symptom asked about only as a 'what if' [P2]. Saying there is NO other symptom ('my other symptoms are none') [P4]. How long each flare or episode lasts [P5]. The activity during which the symptom shows up ('chest pain when running') [P3]. Symptoms that are part of the problem asked about (itching and bumps when asking about hives) [P6]. 'Stomach aches for the past few weeks' counts (how long). 'After travel with lots of walking' counts (event that led up to it). 'Why is my foot hurting' does not (main complaint only). 'For the past few weeks' counts (overall duration); 'only there for a few days then disappears' does not (episode length) [P5]. 'After sleeping' counts (before it started); 'hurts when I bend' does not (when it shows up) [P3]. A headache alongside neck pain counts as another symptom [P6].
After the AI asked The first background information comes in a later message that answers a question the AI asked about the person in the turn just before. Replies to AI questions such as 'have you had other symptoms?', 'how did it start?', 'what are your biggest stressors?'. AI questions that are only section headings ('What happens during sleep apnea?'), which are not asking the person anything. If the AI asked but the person shares a different, unrequested piece of background, it still counts as D2 (they were prompted to say more). AI questions can look like a form with no question mark (for example a list asking for current weight); a reply to that counts as D2 [P9].
On their own later The first background information comes in a later message that the AI did not ask for. Background added without being prompted. Background given in the first message (D1) or right after an AI question about them (D2).
Never shared No background information appears in any of their messages; they only described the main problem. Chats that stay on the main complaint or stay general. Chats with only 'what if' symptoms [P2] or 'no other symptoms' answers [P4]. Any background information at any point (D1 to D3). Describing where the problem is, how it feels or how bad it is does not count as background (it is still Shared more about themselves in column 2).

Rows marked decided by: analyst are your decisions. Rows marked proposed are suggestions waiting for your answer.

column 1 Action wins: a chat with both an understand code and an act code goes to Asking what to do (6144ea17 R1;R3, 69f441ce R2;R5). The action question is what they really want. decided by: analyst
column 2 Column 2 is the person's 2nd message: the next substantive participant message after the coded first message (coded_turn), one code per chat. For the 3 substituted openers this is the message after the substitute. Follows the first-real-message rule from step 07. decided by: analyst

Your decisions

You answered the first 6 questions (rows L5 to L13 above):

  • Thanks-only messages are skipped.
  • A new question wins over background details in column 2.
  • Only background information counts for column 3, and column 3 is renamed.
  • Answering the AI counts as “Shared more about themselves”.
  • “Continued a task” was added for 6929d658.
  • 66aafcc3 is Kept asking to understand, and 671a8337 is Then asked what to do.

What changed: with the background-only rule, With the first message dropped from 16 to 8 chats. Several chats now land in Never shared, because they only described the main problem.

You also approved two small rules (rows L14 and L15):

  1. L14. Recent events or care that led up to the problem count as background, as part of health history. Examples are travel with lots of walking, a doctor visit, a referral or prism glasses.
  2. L15. Describing the main problem in more detail (where it is, how it feels, how bad) is “Shared more about themselves” in column 2, but it is not background for column 3. Those chats end as “Never shared”.

After the pilot (step 12) you approved all 9 proposed edits (rows L16 to L24):

  • Weight, height, activity level and regular habits count as background.
  • A “what if” symptom is not background, so 671a8337 stays Never shared.
  • Something that happened before the problem started (“after sleeping”) is background. The activity when the symptom shows up (“when running”) is not.
  • Saying there are no other symptoms is not background.
  • “How long” means how long the problem has existed overall, not how long each episode lasts.
  • An “other symptom” is one beyond the problem being asked about.
  • A thanks or task fragment such as “Convert to PDF” is ignored, and the rest of the turn is coded.
  • A question to the AI about itself is Kept asking to understand.
  • 6a24b2df was fixed to After the AI asked: the AI had asked for the weight in a form-style list with no question mark.

What changed in the counts: only 6a24b2df moved, from On their own later (now 2) to After the AI asked (now 6).
